content.content:
Applies to the six recorded edges, one prerequisite at a time: read the dependent against each prerequisite in depends_on and apply both criteria to that edge. The evaluation is satisfied only when all six edges pass.

1. License: no element of the dependent contradicts the prerequisite. Fail on any contradicting element — name the element and the prerequisite it departs from.

2. Edge use: in the dependent, find the element whose soundness this prerequisite carries. Fail naming the prerequisite when the dependent contains no such element; an unused recorded edge is a finding, not a licence.

Nothing is pre-named: which element is at issue is what the check discovers at check time, never what the criterion fixes in advance.
content.rationale:
All six recorded prerequisites are inline prose and the dependent is an inline prose commitment, so every one of the six edges falls in the natural-to-natural cell and takes that cell's gate check as its criterion, applied once per recorded prerequisite in turn at check time. A natural-layer child is a commitment in words: the check is non-violation, never behaviour, so it is applied by reading the recorded documents and there is no command to execute and no test path claimed.

Criterion 2 exists because this one evaluation has to carry the coverage of six recorded edges. An evaluation gates the dependent's use of a prerequisite, not the mere absence of a clash with a prerequisite nothing in the dependent invokes; without the second criterion a dependent that never reaches one of its prerequisites would pass that edge vacuously. Which element fails, and against which prerequisite, is the check's output, not part of either criterion.

What each edge carries into the check. The registry parent fixes where a record's fields are kept: one JSON document per handle at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`, the filename the handle, the document the record, no part of it kept anywhere else, and the records found by scanning that directory. A base of the owned set's content identities is a record field, so it is kept and read in that one document; the comparison has no second file or index to consult, and nothing about it is attributed to a change. The surface parent fixes when a record first exists and what opening writes: one draft per named node, each in its own workspace, each record written `open`, each handle and workspace path reported, and no graph state touched. Opening is the moment the base is taken, and the handle the verb mints is what reaches the record afterwards; the no-graph clause bounds what recording a base may write at opening. The record parent fixes the record's identity and what it carries: the handle alone is identity, the node, the edit and the workspace are references, and the record's base content is left to a separate commitment. That deferral is the place this dependent takes — a base is not the record's identity and does not displace the handle, and it is the elsewhere-decided value the parent declines to settle here. The ownership parent fixes which paths are the node's owned set: the node file plus the repo-relative paths in content.ref when ref is an array, only the node file when inline, nothing else. The base is a base over exactly that set, so a base taken over any other content — the working copy's tree, the change's whole tree, paths the node does not own — departs from the parent rather than extending it. The read parent fixes how owned content is read: a node document is read from jj at the change that owns it, under the caller-supplied binary and root. The content the base fixes and the content a landing compares against are read through that read, so a comparison that trusted the working copy's filesystem would be comparing against content the parent says is not the node's. The recording parent fixes what landing is: `record <path>... --to <id>` places the named edits into the node's change, `--to` required, no landing outside an owning change, no node created. The stale refusal stands in front of that recording and names the differing paths within the owned set; the refusal lands nothing, because the recording it guards is the only thing that moves edits into the change.

On the second sentence of the record parent, `everything else a record carries is a reference, not identity`, the reading taken here is that it scopes identity and not the field set: its subject is which carried field could be the record's key, and its answer is the handle alone, the rest being named references to the parts of a draft; the same document lists the record's base content among the commitments decided elsewhere, the recorded lifecycle parent already puts a carried non-reference field on the record, and the recorded registry parent describes the content a record carries as fields of the one document. On that reading a content-identity base is the elsewhere-decided commitment this dependent is, and this edge is where it is cashed. Read instead as forbidding any carried content-identity, the dependent would contradict that parent and criterion 1 would name the element and the prerequisite; the criterion is not narrowed to exclude either reading, and no element is pre-named here.

The check enforces only what the six recorded prerequisites state and presupposes no decision beyond them: the encoding of the base, the exact text of a refusal, and any exit status are not fixed here. It names no element of the dependent, so rewriting the dependent without changing what it decides leaves both criteria intact.
